lines: Born in 1867 in Cincinnati, Ohio, Charles Henry Turner was an early pioneer in the field of insect behavior.
When he was young, he often read about the habits and behavior of insects and became fascinated with this content.
Continuing his study, Turner earned a doctorate in zoology.
He was the first African American to do so.
However, because of racism, he was unable to get a teaching or research position at any major universities.
He moved to St. Louis and taught biology at a high school.
Focusing on research, Turner first discovered that insects are capable of learning.
He found that insects can alter behavior based on previous experience.
In 1923, he died of cardiac disease in Chicago.
During his 33-year career, Turner published more than 70 papers.
His last paper was published the year after his death.
body.text: Born in 1867 in Cincinnati, Ohio, Charles Henry Turner was an early pioneer in the field of insect behavior. When he was young, he often read about the habits and behavior of insects and became fascinated with this content. Continuing his study, Turner earned a doctorate in zoology. He was the first African American to do so. However, because of racism, he was unable to get a teaching or research position at any major universities. He moved to St. Louis and taught biology at a high school. Focusing on research, Turner first discovered that insects are capable of learning. He found that insects can alter behavior based on previous experience. In 1923, he died of cardiac disease in Chicago. During his 33-year career, Turner published more than 70 papers. His last paper was published the year after his death.
